word:lxx:L700089.explanation: This noun means “want of counsel” or “thoughtlessness.” It describes a condition in which a person lacks sound guidance or acts without careful judgment. word:lxx:L700171.explanation: This noun means “purity”—a clean or undefiled condition. It describes the quality of being pure, especially in relation to a person’s life, worship, or dedication. Its precise emphasis in any particular verse depends on the surrounding context, but its central idea remains purity rather than a specific action or object.

word:lxx:L700203.explanation: This noun refers to a person who is the “next of kin”—a close family relative recognized as nearest in family relation. word:lxx:L700346.explanation: Azōbai, also rendered “Azove,” is a personal name rather than a term describing an object, action, or quality. word:lxx:L700412.explanation: This noun means “soot,” the dark powdery substance produced by smoke or burning. word:lxx:L700467.explanation: Airem, also rendered Erem, is a proper name rather than a word describing an action, quality, or object. word:lxx:L700540.explanation: This adjective means “spotless,” describing something free from stain, blemish, or defilement. It presents a condition of cleanness and purity rather than an action. Its exact force in either passage depends on the surrounding verse, but its central idea remains that of being unmarked by anything that would make it impure or flawed.

word:lxx:L700621.explanation: This adjective means “unhindered”: it describes something that is not blocked, restrained, or prevented from proceeding. word:lxx:L700724.explanation: This Greek LXX noun means “threshing,” referring to the work of threshing harvested grain. It names an agricultural activity rather than a person, object, or quality. word:lxx:L700768.explanation: This adjective means “unfading”: it describes something that does not fade or lose its lasting quality. word:lxx:L700786.explanation: This Greek LXX adjective describes something dim, faint, or only dimly seen. It points to limited clarity or reduced brightness rather than something plainly visible. word:lxx:L700863.explanation: This adjective describes someone or something as “unlucky” or “wretched.” It expresses an unfavorable or pitiable condition rather than naming an action. word:lxx:L700881.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means “clothe”: to put clothing on someone or provide covering. word:lxx:L700966.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means “light up,” describing the act of making something shine or become bright. word:lxx:L700988.explanation: This noun means “fortified wall” or “fortification,” referring to a strengthened defensive barrier. word:lxx:L701019.explanation: Anantleō means to go through. It describes passing through a place, as in going through a dry desert.

word:lxx:L701323.explanation: This verb means “hang,” describing the action of hanging someone or something. It expresses an action rather than naming a person, place, or object. word:lxx:L701525.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means to rave or rage with extreme intensity—to express uncontrolled, excessive anger or agitation. The precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself describes furious, unrestrained expression rather than quiet displeasure.

word:lxx:L701590.explanation: This noun refers to a “runaway slave,” and by extension describes “a deserter; rebel.” It identifies someone who has abandoned an obligation, allegiance, or place and is viewed as having turned away. In the Greek Old Testament and related Greek Jewish writings represented by this LXX entity, the word occurs eight times. Its exact force in any verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea is desertion or rebellion against an expected loyalty.

word:lxx:L701716.explanation: This Greek LXX adverb describes something as “lifted up” or situated “on high.” It points to an elevated position or upward direction rather than naming a person, object, or action by itself. word:lxx:L701837.explanation: This Greek LXX noun means “first leader; founder”—someone who begins something and stands at its head. word:lxx:L701842.explanation: This noun means “ruling jailer”: the person who oversees or commands a prison and those held there. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself points to the jail’s governing officer.

word:lxx:L701914.explanation: This noun describes licentiousness—outrageous behavior that rejects proper restraint and moral order. In the Greek Old Testament corpus represented here, it occurs twice: once in Wisdom and once in 3 Maccabees. Its precise force in either passage depends on the surrounding verse and context, but its central meaning remains behavior marked by brazen disregard for what is right and appropriate.

word:lxx:L701958.explanation: Asir is a personal name, not a general word describing an object, action, or quality. In the Greek Old Testament, it identifies a person named Asir. word:lxx:L702007.explanation: Astarteion, also rendered Astartion, is a proper name rather than a common word describing an action, quality, or object. word:lxx:L702072.explanation: Atara is a personal name, referring to a woman or person identified by that name rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. word:lxx:L702199.explanation: This Greek LXX noun means “dismissal” or “forgiveness”: the release of a person, obligation, or offense. word:lxx:L702241.explanation: This Greek LXX interjection can mean “he himself; then.” It may point emphatically to the person himself, or mark a transition to what happens next. word:lxx:L702326.explanation: Aōth, also rendered Aoth, is a personal name rather than a word describing an action, quality, or object. word:lxx:L702384.explanation: This word is a proper name, rendered “Baian” or “Vean.” It identifies a named person or place rather than expressing an action, quality, or abstract idea. word:lxx:L702829.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means to “plunge” or “overwhelm”—to thrust something down into depth or cause it to be overcome.
